headline: CHILE CALLS MINING EMERGENCY AS WINTER STORM TARGETS COPPER BELT — Codelco, Antofagasta, Teck Summoned to Crisis Meeting; 25% of Global Copper Output Faces Disruption Risk
snippet: Chile's Economy and Mining Minister Daniel Mas convened emergency talks July 14 with Codelco, Antofagasta, and Teck Resources as a powerful winter storm tracked toward key copper-producing regions, while regulator Sernageomin activated its crisis committee to monitor landslide and mudslide risk. The storm lashed ten regions from Coquimbo to Biobío, forcing millions indoors; whether rainfall extends far enough north to reach the main mining districts will determine the severity of any production hit. The disruption threat arrives as Chilean output is already under pressure from declining ore grades, water shortages, and the oxide-to-sulfide mining transition — a country that accounts for roughly 25% of world mined copper supplying a market analysts project faces a 330,000–520,000 tonne deficit in 2026.

headline: INDIA SILENCES ITS SILVER MARKET — Import Curbs Drive Premiums to 6-Month High of $6.50/oz; 'Imports Have Nearly Come to a Halt,' Industry CEO Says
snippet: India's restrictions on silver imports have created shortages in the world's largest silver demand market, with premiums over official domestic prices surging to $6.50 per ounce — more than 10% above benchmark — after trading at discounts as deep as $5.50 as recently as May. Chirag Thakkar, CEO of Amrapali Group Gujarat (a leading silver importer), says imports have 'nearly come to a halt, creating a shortage in the Indian market.' India meets more than 80% of its silver demand through overseas purchases, so the curbs set up a structural tension: domestic physical tightness even as lower import volumes could weigh on global silver spot prices and narrow India's trade deficit.

headline: RIO TINTO BETS $15M ON VICUÑA COPPER-GOLD CORRIDOR — Takes ~5% of Mogotes Metals, Grabs 15-Month Exclusivity on Filo Sur; Argentina's Hottest Copper Belt Gets World's #3 Miner Stamp of Approval (TSXV:MOG)
snippet: Mogotes Metals Inc. (TSXV: MOG) announced July 13 that Rio Tinto Exploration Canada will subscribe for 30,387,857 units at C$0.70 per unit — gross proceeds of approximately US$15 million — taking an initial ~5% stake and forming a Strategic & Technical Alliance covering the Filo Sur project in Argentina's Vicuña copper-gold corridor. Rio Tinto receives 15 months of exclusivity on Filo Sur (extendable by six months by mutual agreement), with rights to negotiate deeper joint venture terms; proceeds fund work programs at Filo Sur. The strategic backing by one of the world's three largest mining companies is a significant validation of both the junior and the broader Vicuña district, which has emerged as one of the most watched copper-gold exploration corridors in South America.

headline: ABRASILVER CRACKS OPEN OCULTO WEST: 109m AT 221 g/t SILVER — 14m AT 580 g/t In First Drill Ever Of Gap Zone; Resource Growth Beyond Completed DFS Confirmed at Diablillos, Argentina (TSX:ABRA)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / AbraSilver Resource Corp.
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA) reported July 13 that Phase VI drill hole DDH 26-036 at the Diablillos project in Argentina intersected 109.0 metres at 221.2 g/t silver and 0.72 g/t gold from 114.0 metres depth — including a high-grade core of 14.0 metres at 580 g/t silver — in a previously undrilled gap at Oculto West, confirming broad, high-grade oxide silver-gold mineralization that extends beneath the conceptual open pit outlined in the completed Definitive Feasibility Study. The result directly demonstrates resource growth potential beyond the current DFS mine plan, with Phase VI drilling continuing to test additional undrilled areas and extensions.

headline: FURY GOLD FIRES A THIRD RIG AT EAU CLAIRE — 21m AT 7.01 g/t Au, Including 11m AT 10.27 g/t, Confirms High-Grade Shoot Continuity; James Bay Quebec Discovery Accelerates Into Q4 2026 (TSX:FURY)
snippet: Fury Gold Mines (TSX: FURY) reported July 13 that Phase 2 conversion drill hole 26EC-115 at the Eau Claire gold project in James Bay, Quebec intersected 21.0 metres at 7.01 g/t gold, including 11.0 metres at 10.27 g/t, confirming continuity of the high-grade shoot within the modelled zone. A third diamond drill rig has been mobilized, bringing total active rigs to three — allowing Fury to simultaneously advance resource conversion, follow up on previously high-yielding zones, and continue expansion drilling in Eeyou Istchee Territory through Q4 2026.

headline: FLORIDA MAKES GOLD AND SILVER LEGAL MONEY — Then Buries Dealers in Compliance Paperwork; Industry Calls DeSantis Bill More Bureaucratic Burden Than Monetary Breakthrough
snippet: Florida's law recognizing gold and silver as legal tender took effect July 1, 2026 — but implementation has drawn sharp criticism from the industry it was meant to support. Rather than simply recognizing metals as lawful money, the legislation expanded Florida's Money Services Business framework into the precious-metals marketplace, subjecting coin dealers, depositories, and bullion businesses to new licensing, compliance programs, regular examinations, and reporting obligations. Money Metals Exchange calls it a 'big-government bill attacking Florida's gold industry,' arguing the regulatory burden directly contradicts the law's stated goal of financial freedom and sound money.

headline: GOLD SEEKER ISSUE #72: MINERS ON THE LAUNCHPAD BUT AWAITING ONE CATALYST — GDX Broke Key Resistance, Earnings at Near-Record Levels, Yet Institutional Money Still Sitting Out
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold Seeker Issue #72 surveys a gold and silver mining sector at a critical inflection: the GDX broke above the $42–$46 resistance zone as metals rebounded on soft CPI data, junior and mid-tier miners are generating earnings near all-time highs on $4,000+ gold, and yet institutional positioning remains historically underweight the sector. The weekly roundup frames the July 28-29 Federal Reserve FOMC meeting as the decisive upcoming catalyst — a dovish outcome could unlock the re-rating that mining stock bulls have been forecasting throughout the correction, while another hawkish surprise would extend the standoff between record fundamentals and compressed multiples.
